messages:
alex (support): FYI customer ACME escalated — p95/p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~3-4x over last 30m, they're seeing timeouts and big tail latency. ticket #INC-12481.
juan (eng-runtime): ack. do we have a quick flamegraph or KV cache metrics?
maya (eng-sre): looking at infra metrics now. I see a sharp rise in kv.cache.miss_ratio and prefix_key_cardinality around 23:12 UTC. correlates with a traffic burst from one org id.
juan (eng-runtime): interesting — could be prefix entropy / hot-key amplification. did we recently change prefix normalization?
maya (eng-sre): no deploys to runtime in last 2h. but config push to fronting proxy added a header `X-Client-Region` yesterday. wondering if header got into cache key.
kate (eng-runtime): that would explode keyspace. quick check: logs show many distinct `kv_key` values for same model+prompt slices. sample: `kv_key=model:v1|prefix=<long-uuid>|region=eu-west-1|hdr=X-12345`
juan (eng-runtime): thanks. repro steps to validate:
```bash
# replay a small burst with same headers
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" -H "X-Client-Trace: $RANDOM" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-base","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
this should show kv miss surge in logs and p95 increase.
bob (ingest): also saw prefix warmup queues starved — warmup workers maxed at 100% and eviction rate spiked. looks like warmup can't keep up when key cardinality jumps.
maya (eng-sre): short-term mitigation options: 1) rollback header inclusion if config changed, 2) enable prefix warmup drip (limit new prefixes per-second), 3) temporarily raise cache size for the shard handling that org, 4) route that org to a dedicated pool.
alex (support): customer wants ETA and patch plan. suggested we do 2 + 3 now and follow up? they prefer minimal visible change.
kate (eng-runtime): I can flip warmup drip and bump shard cache.size by 25% for 10m window. prepping a runbook.
juan (eng-runtime): also propose a quick normalization hotfix: sanitize/strip volatile headers from cache key generator before rollout. I'll open PR, but can't ship without thumbs.
maya (eng-sre): implement circuit-breaker for prefix warmup: if distinct-prefix rate > 1000/s, temporarily cap new prefixes to 100/s and mark extra requests as warmup-miss fallback (use small-key fallback hotset). low-risk.
ops-bot: deploy request queued: change=warmup-drip, cache-bump, cb-feature-flag; approvers needed: @juan, @kate
juan (eng-runtime): approving now. running `./scripts/ops/run_change.sh warmup-drip --duration 10m`
kate (eng-runtime): change applied. watch metrics: kv.cache.miss_ratio ->
- before: 0.78
- now: 0.41
p95 backend latency -> down from 980ms to 460ms (prelim).
alex (support): passing update to ACME: applied throttled warmup + cache bump; monitoring. They asked if this is permanent.
bob (ingest): root cause notes for postmortem: one of ACME's clients started sending unique request headers (per-user trace id) that made their request headers transitively part of the cache key; key normalization lacked header whitelist. results: cold-key storm, warmup saturation, eviction churn.
juan (eng-runtime): action items:
- bugfix: sanitize headers in cache-key generation (PR opened: rwd/kv#4567) — owner @juan — high priority
- infra: add size-aware eviction (avoid evicting small hot prefixes) — owner @kate — medium
- runtime: implement prefix-entropy alarm + automated limit (CB) — owner @maya — high
- docs: support guidance on header best-practices + example repro — owner @alex — low
- postmortem and customer note — owner @alex — due EOD
maya (eng-sre): can we also add a metric `kv.new_prefix_rate` and alert at 200/s? will help detect early.
juan (eng-runtime): yes. I'll add instrument and dashboard.
kate (eng-runtime): follow-up: PR for normalization includes unit tests and an opt-in flag. will schedule hotfix deploy in next 30m after tests pass.
alex (support): ACME acknowledged and reduced rate from their side while we patch. they're satisfied for now but want permanent fix.
bob (ingest): leaving a note: if we add header-stripping be sure to keep `Authorization` or customer-specified key fields if they purposely wanted per-user caching. include whitelist approach.
juan (eng-runtime): agreed. whitelist-based normalization + explicit `cacheHint` header for customers.
maya (eng-sre): monitoring looks stable last 10m. p99 still slightly elevated but trending down. will keep this thread open until p99 within baseline for 1h.
alex (support): thumbs up. I'll update ticket INC-12481 with mitigation timeline and owners.
kate (eng-runtime): marking postmortem owner @juan and SRE reviewer @maya. drafting root cause summary now.
juan (eng-runtime): quick log snippet for PM:
```
2026-03-17T23:12:05Z runtime INFO kv_key="model:v1|prefix:user:abcd...|hdr=X-User-Trace:9a3f" miss=true
2026-03-17T23:12:06Z runtime INFO kv_warmup_enqueue prefix=user:abcd... queue_len=980
2026-03-17T23:12:07Z runtime WARN eviction loop: evicting 120 keys, free=12MB
```
maya (eng-sre): thanks. good job team.
ops-bot: change complete: warmup-drip, cache-bump, cb-feature-flag.
juan (eng-runtime): closing for now. will post postmortem link here when ready.
